e-12389.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}y+x{z}^{2}\,dz\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}y+x{z}^{2}\,dz]dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{[{x}^{2}yz+\frac{x{z}^{3}}{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}y(1-0)+x(\frac{1}{3}-0)\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{3}x\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{3}x\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{3}x\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}y+\frac{1}{6}{x}^{2}]}_{x=-1}^{x=2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{3}y({2}^{3}-(-1)^{3})+\frac{1}{6}({2}^{2}-(-1)^{2}))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}3y+\frac{1}{2}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}3y+\frac{1}{2}\,dx & ={[\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{y}{2}]}_{y=1}^{y=2} \\  & =(6+1)-(\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

e-12368.knowledge_point: Evaluating Repeated Integrals Over Non-Rectangular Domains
e-12368.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-y}x\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}[{\int }_{0}^{3-x-y}x\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}x\cdot [z]_{z=0}^{z=3-x-y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}x(3-x-y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x-{x}^{2}-xy\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x-{x}^{2}-xy\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{x}3x-{x}^{2}-xy\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(3x-{x}^{2})y-\frac{1}{2}x{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3x-{x}^{2})(x-0)-\frac{1}{2}x({x}^{2}-0)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}{x}^{3}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}{x}^{3}\,dx & ={[{x}^{3}-\frac{3}{8}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =8-6 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

e-12390.knowledge_point: Evaluating Repeated Integrals Using the Sum and Product Rules
e-12390.worked_solution:
Since the domain of integration $R = [1,2] \times \left[0,\pi/2\right] \times [1,4]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡y}{x}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{dx}{x}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy{\int }_{1}^{4}dz\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}\,dx{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy\,{\int }_{1}^{4}dz & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|]_{1}^{2}\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /2}\cdot (4-1) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))\cdot 3 \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-0)\cdot (0+1)\cdot 3 \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\int_{1}^{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{1}^{4} \dfrac{\sin{y}}{x} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x = 3\ln 2.
$$

decision.explanation: Integrating with respect to x gives 1/3-y+y^2+sin(z). Integrating over z from 0 to 2π gives 2π(1/3-y+y^2), since the sine integral is zero. Finally, integrating over y from 0 to 1 gives 2π(1/3-1/2+1/3)=π/3.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-y)^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-y)^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{[\frac{(x-y)^{3}}{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z[x]_{x=0}^{x=1}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-y)^{3}}{3}-\frac{(0-y)^{3}}{3}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z(1-0)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}[z]_{z=0}^{z=2\pi }+[-\operatorname{cos}⁡z]_{z=0}^{z=2\pi })\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}(2\pi -0)+(-1+1))\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\pi }{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}\text{d}y & =\frac{2\pi }{3}{[-\frac{(1-y)^{4}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}((-0+\frac{1}{4})-(-\frac{1}{4}+0)) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}xy+yz+xz\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2}xy+yz+xz\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2}(y+z)x+yz\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y+z)\,{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2}+yz[x]_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y+z)(2-0)+yz(2-0)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}2(y+z)+2yz\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y$, treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}2(y+z)+2yz\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2(y+z)+2yz\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2(1+z)y+2z\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}((1+z)[{y}^{2}]_{1}^{2}+2z[y]_{1}^{2})\,\text{d}z \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}((1+z)(4-1)+2z(2-1))\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3(1+z)+2z)\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3+5z)\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3+5z)\text{d}z & ={[3z+\frac{5}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3(1-0)+\frac{5}{2}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integrating over x gives 1/3+y². Integrating over y from 0 to 2 gives 2/3+8/3=10/3. The integrand is independent of z, so integrating from −1 to 1 multiplies this by 2, giving 20/3.

after.worked_solution:
First, we apply the sum rule and write our repeated integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,1]\times [0,2]\times [-1,1]$ is a rectangular box, and each integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our sum of repeated integrals as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z\,+\,{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z
$$

Let's evaluate each of these separately:

- For the first product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z & ={[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1}\cdot (2-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z & =(1-0)\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{8}{3}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{16}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z=\frac{4}{3}+\frac{16}{3}=\frac{20}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integrating over z gives x²[sin(y+π)−sin(y)]=−2x²sin(y). Integrating over y from 0 to π/2 gives −2x². Finally, integrating over x from 1 to 2 gives −2(8−1)/3=−14/3.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z)]_{z=0}^{z=\pi }\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+0))\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,dy\,dx \\  & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy\,dx & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy]dx \\  & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{y=0}^{y=\pi /2}\,dx \\  & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}(-0+1)\,dx \\  & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\,dx & =-2{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{x=1}^{x=2} \\  & =-2(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =-\frac{14}{3}.\end{aligned}

decision.explanation: For z>0, the inner integral is [arctan(x/z)] from 0 to √3z, giving π/3. Thus the remaining integrals give ∫₀²(πy/3) dy = 2π/3. The singularity at x=z=0 does not change the convergent integral.

after.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}z}\frac{z}{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}z}\frac{z}{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y}{[z\cdot \frac{1}{z}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{z})]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{3}z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y}{[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{z})]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{3}z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y}\operatorname{arctan}⁡\sqrt{3}-\operatorname{arctan}⁡0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y}\frac{\pi }{3}\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z,$ treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y}\frac{\pi }{3}\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{y}\frac{\pi }{3}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[\frac{\pi }{3}{\int }_{0}^{y}dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\pi }{3}[z]_{z=0}^{z=y}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot y\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\pi }{3}\,y\,dy & =\frac{\pi }{3}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}(2-0) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}\end{aligned}

decision.explanation: Integrating over x gives cos(y+z)−cos(2y+z). Integrating over y from 0 to z gives sin(2z)−sin(3z)/2−sin(z)/2. Integrating over z from 0 to π/2 yields 1−1/6−1/2=1/3.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}{\int }_{0}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dx\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}[{\int }_{0}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dx]dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y+z)]_{x=0}^{x=y}\,dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+y+z)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0+y+z)\,dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+z)\,dy\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+z)\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{z}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+z)\,dy]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y+z)]}_{y=0}^{y=z}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(z+z)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2z+z)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0+z)+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0+z)\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡3z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡3z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz & ={[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2z+\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡3z+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z]}_{z=0}^{z=\pi /2} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})]-[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡0+\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡0+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡0] \\  & =[\frac{1}{2}+0+0]-[-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+z)\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{z}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+z)\,dy]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y+z)]}_{y=0}^{y=z}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(z+z)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2z+z)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0+z)+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0+z)\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡3z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz\end{aligned}

$$

decision.explanation: Integrating over x gives yz(y+z)². Integrating over y from 0 to z gives z(z⁴/4+2z⁴/3+z⁴/2)=17z⁵/12. Finally, integrating over z from 0 to 2 gives (17/12)(64/6)=136/9.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{z}{\int }_{0}^{y+z}2xyz\,dx\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{z}[{\int }_{0}^{y+z}2xyz\,dx]dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{z}[{x}^{2}yz]_{x=0}^{x=y+z}\,dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{z}(y+z)^{2}yz\,dy\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $z$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{z}(y+z)^{2}yz\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{z}{y}^{3}z+2{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+y{z}^{3}\,dy]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}z+\frac{2}{3}{y}^{3}{z}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=z}\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{4}{z}^{5}+\frac{2}{3}{z}^{5}+\frac{1}{2}{z}^{5}\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{17}{12}{z}^{5}\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{17}{12}{z}^{5}\,dz & ={[\frac{17}{72}{z}^{6}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{17}{72}\cdot 64 \\  & =\frac{136}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: For z>0, integrating over y gives x[sin(y/z)]₀^{z²}=x sin(z). Integrating over z from 0 to π/2 gives x. Finally, ∫₋₁⁰ x dx=−1/2. The endpoint at z=0 is handled by the convergent improper integral.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{{z}^{2}}\frac{x}{z}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{z})\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{{z}^{2}}\frac{x}{z}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{z})\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{[\frac{x}{z}\cdot z\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{z})]}_{y=0}^{y={z}^{2}}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{z})]}_{y=0}^{y={z}^{2}}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x(\operatorname{sin}⁡z-\operatorname{sin}⁡0)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[-x\operatorname{cos}⁡z]_{z=0}^{z=\pi /2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}x(-0+1)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}x\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}{\int }_{0}^{x+z}(72xyz)\,dy\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36xz[{\int }_{0}^{x+z}2y\,dy]dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36xz[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=x+z}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36xz(x+z)^{2}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36{x}^{3}z+72{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+36x{z}^{3}\,dx\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x,$ treating $z$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36{x}^{3}z+72{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+36x{z}^{3}\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{z}36{x}^{3}z+72{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+36x{z}^{3}\,dx]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[9{x}^{4}z+24{x}^{3}{z}^{2}+18{x}^{2}{z}^{3}]_{x=0}^{x=z}\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}51{z}^{5}\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}51{z}^{5}\,dz & ={[\frac{17{z}^{6}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{17}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}{\int }_{0}^{x+z}(72xyz)\,dy\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36xz[{\int }_{0}^{x+z}2y\,dy]dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36xz[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=x+z}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36xz(x+z)^{2}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36{x}^{3}z+72{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+36x{z}^{3}\,dx\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x,$ treating $z$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36{x}^{3}z+72{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+36x{z}^{3}\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{z}36{x}^{3}z+72{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+36x{z}^{3}\,dx]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[9{x}^{4}z+24{x}^{3}{z}^{2}+18{x}^{2}{z}^{3}]_{x=0}^{x=z}\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}51{z}^{5}\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}51{z}^{5}\,dz & ={[\frac{17{z}^{6}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{17}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we apply the sum rule and write our repeated integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}x{y}^{2}{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,4]\times [1,2]\times [0,1]$ is a rectangular box, and each integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our sum of repeated integrals as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z-{\int }_{0}^{4}\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}z\,\text{d}z
$$

Let's evaluate each of these separately:

- For the first product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{4}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{1}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{z}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(8-0)(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{3})(\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =8(\frac{7}{3})(\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{14}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}z\,\text{d}z & =(4-0)\cdot (2-1)\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x{y}^{2}{z}^{3}-z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x=\frac{14}{3}-2=\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we apply the sum rule and write our repeated integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{y}{z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,\pi ]\times [0,2]\times [1,e]$ is a rectangular box, and each integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our sum of repeated integrals as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{e}\text{d}z+{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{z}\,\text{d}z
$$

Let's evaluate each of these separately:

- For the first product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{e}\text{d}z & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{0}^{\pi }\cdot (2-0)\cdot (e-1) \\  & =(1+1)\cdot 2\cdot (e-1) \\  & =4(e-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{z}\,\text{d}z & =(\pi -0)\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot [\operatorname{ln}⁡|z|]_{1}^{e} \\  & =\pi \cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{y}{z})\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x=4(e-1)+2\pi =2(2e+\pi -2).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\int }_{2}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z-{\int }_{2}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}4x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,1]\times [1,2]\times [2,5]$ is a rectangular box, and each integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our sum of repeated integrals as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{2}^{5}\text{d}z-{\int }_{0}^{1}4x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{2}^{5}\text{d}z
$$

Let's evaluate each of these separately:

- For the first product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{2}^{5}\text{d}z & =(1-0)\cdot [{y}^{3}]_{1}^{2}\cdot (5-2) \\  & =1\cdot (8-1)\cdot 3 \\  & =3\cdot 7 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{-1}^{1}2z\,\text{d}z & =(1-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot [{z}^{2}]_{-1}^{1} \\  & =1\cdot 2\cdot 0 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}

$$
